chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “A man may have a eunuch who enters upon his women and hands them water for wudu (ablution), and so he sees their hair?” He said: “No.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution) water or the act of ablution in context
key_terms.لَا: a ruling of prohibition or negation in response to the question

ai.seo_question: Can a eunuch servant enter upon women of the household and see their hair while assisting with wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning household privacy and the limits of what may be seen by a eunuch servant in relation to a man's women. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام answers in the negative, indicating that such entry and viewing of their hair is not permitted.
